title: The night walk
summary: A group of students climb a mountain in the dark to watch the sun come up, but the weather has other plans.
paragraphs: The plan sounded perfect when their teacher explained it: leave the camp at three in the morning, walk for two hours with head torches and reach the top of the mountain in time to see the sunrise. Fourteen students raised their hands immediately. At three o'clock, standing in the cold, only half of them looked so {{enthusiastic}}.

The path was steep and full of loose stones. Nobody talked much. Each person followed the circle of light in front of them and listened to the sound of their own breathing. Once, the guide stopped and turned off his torch. "Look up," he whispered. The sky was so full of stars that it looked {{unreal}}, like a painting.

Half an hour from the top, the wind changed. A thick grey cloud came up from the valley and covered everything. The temperature dropped and a light rain began to fall. The guide checked the map, talked to the teacher and made a decision. "We aren't going to the top," he said. "It isn't safe. We'll wait in the {{shelter}} and go down when it's light."

There was a groan of disappointment. The shelter was a small stone hut with a wooden bench. They sat close together, shared chocolate and told the worst jokes they knew. Someone started singing, and soon everyone was singing, badly and loudly.

When the cloud finally lifted at eight o'clock, there was no sunrise to see, just a wet, bright morning and a view across three valleys. Nobody complained. Years later, when they met again, they didn't remember the mountain or the view. They remembered the hut, the songs and the strange {{warmth}} of being together on a cold morning when the plan went wrong.

enthusiastic.meaning: showing a lot of interest and excitement

unreal.meaning: so strange or beautiful that it does not seem real

shelter.meaning: a small building that protects people from bad weather

warmth.meaning: a pleasant feeling of being warm, or of friendship

questions.question: How did some students feel at three o'clock?
options: Less enthusiastic than when they raised their hands
questions.explanation: At three o'clock only half of them looked as enthusiastic as before.

questions.question: Why did the guide turn off his torch?
options: So the students could see the stars
questions.explanation: He turned it off and told them to look up at the sky full of stars.

questions.question: Why didn't the group reach the top?
options: A cloud, wind and rain made it unsafe.
questions.explanation: A thick cloud came, the temperature dropped and the guide said it wasn't safe.

questions.question: What did the students remember years later?
options: The time together in the hut
questions.explanation: They remembered the hut, the songs and being together.
